text:
emma: Heads up — since the VPC egress tighten went live in apac-1 we've seen the GPU warm pool fail to reach target. Keystore/KMS decrypts are timing out and nodes are stuck in Init.

ops-bot: ALERT keystore.decrypt.errors >= 5/min (apac-1) — sample: keystore-connector: KMS 504 from kms.apac-1.redwood-kms.internal

danielle: yep noticed. affect started ~2801112200, correlation with egress deny applied to 10.18.0.0/16 nat gw.

theo: can we get a quick stack trace / logs? what's failing first: KMS IAM auth or network only?

emma: logs show network timeouts, then KMS client returns "context deadline exceeded". no auth denied entries in KMS audit. looks like traffic not leaving through PrivateLink.

alex: putting it bluntly — we locked down IGW/NAT paths to reduce cross-account egress. result: keystore can't reach regional KMS endpoint. we can either relax egress for the keystore subnet or route keystore -> privatelink. tradeoffs: NAT throughput cost vs private link (VPCE) per-hour and endpoint ENI limits.

priya: cost numbers: extra NAT GW + data processed estimate for current load ~ $1.8k/month. VPCE + interface endpoints + ENI limits across nodes ~ $800/mo but higher ops complexity and quota requests. Also audit logs for KMS cross-account calls increase S3 storage by ~20%.

danielle: compliance asked for egress deny by default though. Can we carve an exception just for keystore service? short term P0: add egress allow to kms.apac-1 for keystore subnet. medium: migrate to privatelink + regional KMS replica or envelope keys cached locally.

theo: agreed. Short term: add egress allow rule, but scoped to IPs/tags. Also add circuit-breaker in keystore to fall back to cached envelope keys to allow nodes to bootstrap (TTL 10m).

emma: example egress rule we're proposing:
```
- Allow: tcp 443 to kms.apac-1.redwood-kms.internal (resolved IPs)
- Source: sg-keystore-apac
- Comment: temporary exception for node bootstrap; remove once privatelink done
```

emma: also posting a log snippet: `keystore: dial tcp 10.200.34.12:443: i/o timeout` then `keystore: decrypt err: context deadline exceeded (after 30s)`

alex: on the caching idea — we already have envelope-key flow for runtime tokens but not for node bootstrap. Adding ephemeral node-encrypted keys means less KMS calls per node. Cost drop is significant (estimated 60% fewer decrypts). work effort: ~3 days infra + 1 day security review.

priya: security note: any local envelope key cache increases blast radius if node compromised. need HSM-backed wrapping keys and strict TTL + rotation. Also add audit log marker when cache used vs live decrypt.

danielle: ops plan: 1) emergency egress allow for keystore subnet (timeboxed 72h) 2) implement circuit-breaker + cached envelope keys (canary in staging) 3) request VPCE quota and design privatelink route 4) follow-up to revert egress allow.

emma: can someone run the quick rollback/allow change? I can own the circuit-breaker work.

alex: I'll open a short-lived ACL change PR and tag @security for expedited review. putting a TTL on the rule.

ops-bot: ACTION created ticket INF-5532: "keystore egress exception + bootstrap cache" assigned to alex, due 2801112359

priya: +1 for audit markers. please add a field `keystore_bootstrap=kms_cache|live` in our request logs. we'll need that in the eval dashboard.

theo: also want an extra metric for `keystore.decrypt.latency` so we can alert earlier if privatelink starts throttling.

danielle: ok i'll schedule the rule change in the noon maintenance window (apac time) and post the PR link here once ready.

emma: thanks — i'll start the feature branch for in-memory envelope cache and doc the security controls.

alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/402 — contains the ACL change and IP list. tagging @priya for cross-check on IP ranges.

priya: reviewed ACL, looks scoped. request we add an expiry tag `redwood:expiry=2801140000` so infra can auto-clean if we forget.

emma: good call. will land the cache prototype to staging after tests.

theo: follow-up: once privatelink is provisioned, let's measure per-decrypt latency and cost and decide permanent path. for now emergency allow + cache seems safest.

danielle: noted, closing thread once ACL is in and envelope cache is canaried. thanks team :thumbsup:
